Metadata.title: Juan Antonio Gómez Gil — Software Engineer
Metadata.description: Frontend-focused Software Engineer. I investigate complex contexts, connect systems and build technically viable solutions.

Hero.body1: Specialized in frontend, I work beyond the interface to turn product complexity into technical decisions that can be built.
Hero.body2: I investigate context, make constraints explicit and connect design, backend and business to take the solution from the initial conversation through production.

Process.title: <line>From client to production:</line><line>clarity before code,</line><line>evidence before calling it done.</line>
Process.titleLabel: From client to production: clarity before code, evidence before calling it done.
Process.intro: These are not isolated stages or a list of capabilities. They form one system that adds context, connects ownership and ends with evidence in production.
Process.storyLabel: Progressive assembly of an engineering system

aiBridge.question: How do I keep my focus and energy closer to client work and away from repetitive code?

understand.title: Do not assume. Ask.
understand.question: The client request starts the conversation; it does not define the solution.
understand.body: I listen to the client and align the goal, user, product constraints and definition of success before turning a conversation into technical work.

investigate.title: Make the contract explicit.
investigate.question: If the criteria are not shared, implementation is a gamble.
investigate.body: I turn ambiguity into scope, states, design decisions, data, ownership and acceptance criteria that the whole team can verify.

connect.title: Follow the whole flow.
connect.question: The problem does not end where the ticket does.
connect.body: I trace how a decision travels through content, CMS, APIs, frontend and operations. I make ownership and dependencies visible.

propose.title: Decide where it lives.
propose.question: Every responsibility needs a place and a reason.
propose.body: I frame alternatives, expose trade-offs and choose the simplest solution that addresses the cause without creating unnecessary debt.

build.title: Build for the real world.
build.question: The happy path is not the product.
build.body: I turn the decision into maintainable architecture and treat states, errors, accessibility and performance as part of the product, not finishing touches.

validate.title: Validate what matters.
validate.question: Without evidence, done is only an opinion.
validate.body: I use cross-system debugging, tests, edge cases and reviewable evidence to verify the behaviour of the whole system before calling it done.

deliver.title: Prove it in production.
deliver.body: I take the solution through release, observe its behaviour, close the loop with the teams involved and leave behind the knowledge required to maintain it.

Case.title: Connecting teams is also part of the solution.
Case.intro: Three different problems. One way of working: understand the whole system, make criteria explicit and shorten the distance between a decision and a valid implementation.

ai.titleLine2: More time for the work that creates value.

context.title: Versioned context
context.description: Decisions, rules and system maps live beside the code. Agents and skills load only the information each task needs, without relying on individual memory or endless prompts.

criteria.title: Governed workflows
criteria.description: A registry connects every change to specialists, documentation, boundaries, risk and checks. AI does not improvise the process: it follows versioned routes proportional to impact.

implementation.title: Automated validation
implementation.description: Documentation, contracts, fixtures, integrations and rules are audited during development. Drift appears before review, while it is still inexpensive to correct.

evidence.title: Reviewable evidence
evidence.description: Each delivery produces persistent reports, summaries and results. Reviewers receive scope, decisions and verifiable checks, not only a diff and a reconstructed explanation.

ai.statement: AI does not replace the engineering process. It connects to it to work with context, boundaries and evidence.

hic.metaTitle: HIC case — AI and an engineering operating system
hic.metaDescription: How I connected CMS, APIs, frontend, documentation and AI to create living acceptance criteria and verifiable evidence.
hic.label: HIC · AI APPLIED TO THE ENGINEERING WORKFLOW
hic.title: Turning scattered knowledge into a project operating system.
hic.intro: The challenge was not writing code faster. It was enabling product, design and engineering to decide and implement from the same context.
hic.problemTitle: The complexity lived between systems —and between teams.
hic.problemBody1: The platform is built from dynamic CMS content, API contracts, data transformations and a component runtime. A seemingly local decision can cross every one of those layers.
hic.problemBody2: Some knowledge lived in conversations, tickets or individual people. That made it harder to detect impact, keep documentation aligned and define when an implementation was truly done.
hic.systemTitle: AI connects to the process with context, boundaries and evidence.
hic.systemIntro: I designed a working layer around the repository: it does not decide for the team or replace sources of truth; it organizes the required context and runs reproducible checks.

context.title: Context on demand
context.body: Specialized agents and skills load relevant route, CMS, API, component or accessibility knowledge according to the task.

criteria.title: Living acceptance criteria
criteria.body: Requirements become concrete contracts and checks that evolve with the code and clarify what done well means.

docs.title: Documentation as code
docs.body: Decisions, flows and ownership are versioned and validated to reduce the gap between documentation and the running product.

evidence.title: Dynamic evidence
evidence.body: Fixtures, integration audits, comparisons and local reports turn assumptions into reviewable results before a PR is opened.

map.title: Knowledge map
map.body: Routes, content types, models, transformations, components, tests and docs are related to anticipate the impact radius of a change.

hic.decisionsTitle: Automate the repeatable work to protect judgement.
hic.decisionsBody: The system uses bounded task catalogues, typed inputs and explicit sources of truth. It separates configuration, execution and results, avoids generic context-free instructions and keeps every validation traceable.
hic.resultTitle: Less uncertain delivery and higher-value conversations.
hic.resultBody: The outcome is a workflow that detects mismatches earlier, reduces search and rework, prepares more consistent handoffs and shortens the path from requirement to validation. Recovered time goes back to what matters most: connecting teams and making better decisions.

figma.metaTitle: Figma plugin case — Design connected to Salesforce
figma.metaDescription: A plugin that turns Figma components and Excel data into HTML emails ready for Salesforce.
figma.label: FIGMA PLUGIN · DESIGN TO PRODUCTION
figma.title: Turning a visual system into a delivery tool.
figma.intro: The goal was to remove manual reconstruction between design and campaign without losing control over components, data or the final HTML.
figma.problemTitle: Designing the email was only part of the work.
figma.problemBody1: Every campaign had to follow a catalogue of blocks, metadata and regional variants while producing HTML compatible with the real constraints of the channel.
figma.problemBody2: When design, data and publishing live in separate tools, manual tasks, copy errors and differences appear between the approved piece and the asset that reaches production.
figma.systemTitle: Figma becomes the interface to a controlled pipeline.
figma.systemIntro: The plugin imports approved components, lets users compose a piece in an exportable frame and orchestrates the transformations required for delivery.

library.title: Controlled library
library.body: Available blocks are imported from a shared library and instantiated with consistent structure and metadata.

composition.title: Assisted composition
composition.body: Users build the campaign inside a plugin-managed frame with navigation, selection and context checks.

data.title: Data from Excel
data.body: Spreadsheet uploads bring links and variants through the backend instead of transferring information manually.

transform.title: HTML transformation
transform.body: Each component has specific renderers and normalization rules to generate an email that matches both design and channel.

delivery.title: Salesforce delivery
delivery.body: The same workflow previews or downloads the HTML and creates the Salesforce asset with its category and metadata.

figma.decisionsTitle: Good automation starts by bounding the system.
figma.decisionsBody: Rather than attempting to export any design, the pipeline works with known components and specific transformations. That constraint provides autonomy without giving up quality.
figma.resultTitle: Less reconstruction between the approved and published piece.
figma.resultBody: Design, content and delivery are connected in one journey. The team can reuse blocks, apply data and produce assets more consistently, reserving review time for visual and content decisions.

racing.metaTitle: On Racing case — Strava, progress and learning
racing.metaDescription: A gamified academy connecting Strava activity with progress, lessons, coaches and rewards.
racing.label: ON RACING · DATA-CONNECTED PRODUCT
racing.title: Turning sports activity into progress users can feel.
racing.intro: The experience had to connect real training, content and motivation without exposing users to the complexity of an external API.
racing.problemTitle: External activity had to become product state.
racing.problemBody1: The academy combines video and audio lessons, coaches, weekly challenges and rewards. But progress depends on activity happening outside the application and arriving from Strava.
racing.problemBody2: That means solving authentication, token refresh, webhooks, scheduled synchronization, API limits and data consistency before showing a reliable progress bar.
racing.systemTitle: Data, content and motivation work as one journey.
racing.systemIntro: The application translates sports events into persistent progress and uses that state to unlock localized content and rewards.

identity.title: Connected identity
identity.body: OAuth links the athlete to the application and handles credential refresh without turning it into an interface concern.

sync.title: Resilient synchronization
sync.body: Webhooks and scheduled processes update activities, account for retries and limits, and invalidate data when the source changes.

model.title: Progress model
model.body: Users, activities, weeks, lessons and rewards are related in the database to keep state coherent.

experience.title: Learning experience
experience.body: Video, audio, coaches and unlockable content turn sports data into an experience with continuity.

signals.title: Product signals
signals.body: Analytics and observability make both user behavior and failures in critical integrations visible.

racing.decisionsTitle: The integration should absorb complexity, not pass it on.
racing.decisionsBody: The product separates Strava communication, persistence and experience. The interface consumes stable state while integration layers handle expiry, failures and updates.
racing.resultTitle: A continuous experience built on systems that are not.
racing.resultBody: User activity becomes visible progress, access to content and rewards. Product, data and training stay connected without exposing the operational complexity that sustains the experience.

Tools.title: They are tools.
Tools.statement: The capability is understanding systems and solving problems.

About.title: I like working where the answer is not clear yet.
About.body1: I started by specializing in frontend, but my work has progressively moved toward more transversal problems.
About.body2: I want to understand the whole product: from the initial need to the data, APIs, architecture and final experience.
About.body3: I especially enjoy problems that require investigation, conversations across disciplines and decisions before writing code.
About.statement: My goal is not simply to implement a solution. It is to make the problem disappear.
